answer: Tie each identity to one real electric car. First, onboarding registers a VIN with the charging network and checks it against the vehicle registry, one VIN per identity. Second, each epoch the agent submits a fresh charging receipt signed by a public charger, with location and kilowatt-hours. Third, a VIN backing two identities is blacklisted and its deposit slashed. A used EV costs about 8,000 dollars, so fielding 1,000 fake identities means 8 million dollars in cars. A hollow fleet with no real opal gleam of use burns out fast, while honest agents keep their ember of work alive.
